title: I paid $67 in fees to lose $85. Here’s the math I skipped.
author: luwihu
selftext:
My fee rate is 0.092% per side. Measured against what I actually risk, it was closer to 37%.

Same fee. Different denominator. That difference explains a bot failure I spent three weeks blaming on everything else.

You don’t risk your position size. You risk the distance from entry to stop. 

So measure the fee the same way:    
fee in R = 2 × fee rate ÷ stop distance

Two, because you pay going in and coming out. That’s the whole formula.

Two of my bots, same exchange, same week:

Bot A, stops 4 to 9% wide: 0.02 to 0.05R per round trip.

Bot B, stops 0.5 to 1.5% wide: 0.13 to 0.38R.

Real trades, not hypotheticals. Bot A paid 20 cents in and 18 cents out, risking $19. Bot B paid $1.09 in and $1.10 out, risking $5.90.

Now the part that actually hurt. Bot B targeted 1:1. Win one unit, lose one unit, hand over 0.37 units every round trip. 

Break even win rate isn’t 50%.    
It’s 68%!!!

I built something that needed to be right two times out of three just to stay flat, and then went looking for bugs in the entry logic.

30 day numbers:

Bot B did $72,371 of volume on an $846 account. 85x turnover. $67 in fees. Lost $85. So 78% of what that “losing strategy” lost, it never lost to the market. It paid to the exchange.

Bot A did $7,469 of volume on $1,175. 6.4x turnover. $6.87 in fees, made $42.    
Turnover is the fee bill. Timeframe drives turnover. So your timeframe is your fee bill, and nobody puts that on the comparison chart.

Two things that surprised me while digging:

My exchange’s realized PnL column is gross of fees. I checked one trade: size × price move equalled the displayed number exactly, with $1.23 of fees sitting somewhere else entirely. So what I’d been reading as profit was profit before paying to make it. Wallet balance is the only honest source.

Maker orders fix this on paper and not in practice. Resting a limit order instead of crossing the spread flips the cost, which is close to free money for a slow strategy that can afford to wait. Useless for a 15 minute signal, where a missed fill isn’t a slightly worse entry, it’s a missed trade.

Bot B is paused now. Not because the signal was bad. Because the arithmetic was against it before the first trade.    
If you run anything scalp adjacent on a taker fee venue, do the division. Takes 30 seconds. 

It might explain something you’ve been blaming on your entries.
